_meta.indication: CRENESSITY is indicated as adjunctive treatment to glucocorticoid replacement to control androgens in adults and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2:1 (active:placebo), 24-week double-blind period followed by open-label treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with classic CAH due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency requiring supraphysiologic glucocorticoid doses (>13 mg/m2/day hydrocortisone equivalents)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline in glucocorticoid daily dose at Week 24 while Week 24 androstenedione levels are controlled (≤120% of baseline or ≤ULN for age and sex)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean percent change in glucocorticoid daily dose at Week 24 was -27.3% (crinecerfont) vs -10.3% (placebo); difference -17.0% (95% CI -23.8, -10.2; p<0.0001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2:1 (active:placebo), 28-week double-blind period followed by open-label treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Children aged 4 to 17 years with classic CAH due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency requiring supraphysiologic glucocorticoid doses (>12 mg/m2/day hydrocortisone equivalents)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in serum androstenedione level at Week 4 while glucocorticoid dose is stable
pivotal_trials.result: Serum androstenedione at Week 4 decreased by -197 (39.4) ng/dL with crinecerfont vs an increase of 71 (56.2) ng/dL with placebo; treatment difference -268 (95% CI: -403, -132)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions in adults (≥4%): fatigue (25% vs 15% placebo), headache (16% vs 15%), dizziness (8% vs 3%), arthralgia (7% vs 0%), back pain (6% vs 3%), decreased appetite (4% vs 2%), myalgia (4% vs 3%). In pediatric patients: headache (25% vs 6%), abdominal pain (13% vs 0%), fatigue (7% vs 0%), nasal congestion (7% vs 3%), epistaxis (4% vs 0%). Serious concern is acute adrenal insufficiency/adrenal crisis (adrenal crisis 1.6% with crinecerfont vs 0% placebo in adults).
target_moa: Crinecerfont is a selective first-in-class antagonist of the corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1) receptor; it binds CRF1 receptors and inhibits ACTH secretion from the pituitary, thereby reducing excessive production of adrenal androgens.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this application because the application did not raise efficacy, safety, or other issues requiring input from external experts.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy designation granted December 1, 2023; met criteria based on preliminary clinical data showing statistically significant reductions in total daily glucocorticoid dose requirements while maintaining control of adrenal androgen levels compared to placebo.

citations.quote: Crinecerfont has Orphan (March 15, 2019), Fast Track (June 15, 2021), and Breakthrough Therapy (December 1, 2023) designations. Crinecerfont met breakthrough therapy designation criteria because the Applicant submitted preliminary clinical data showing that the drug may provide a substantial improvement over available therapy based on statistically significant
reductions in total daily glucocorticoid dose requirements (in many cases to physiologic doses) while maintaining control of adrenal androgen levels with crinecerfont compared to placebo.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug designation granted March 15, 2019 for the treatment of classic CAH.

summary.text: Crinecerfont, a first-in-class CRF1 receptor antagonist, holds Orphan (2019), Fast Track (2021), and Breakthrough Therapy (2023) designations and was granted priority review; it received full (traditional) approval based on two pivotal phase 3 placebo-controlled trials in adults and children with classic CAH.

requirement.text: 4738-1 Perform a lactation study (milk only or mother-infant pair study) in lactating women who have received Crenessity to measure concentrations of crinocerfont and its major metabolites in breast milk using a validated assay and to assess the effects on the breastfed infant, if a mother-infant pair study is conducted.

requirement.text: 4738-2 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Crenessity during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, and adverse effects on the developing fetus, neonate, and infant. Assess infant outcomes through at least the first year of life. The study should also collect adverse event data for lactating women and infants exposed to Crenessity through breastfeeding to assess for any potential risks to the infant from breastfeeding. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol
